description: Solo participant working on space health monitoring and anomaly detection using Python and Streamlit.
summary:
SpaceHealth-Sentinel is an interactive scientific research platform designed to explore biological risks associated with human spaceflight and investigate potential potential preventive countermeasures.
The application uses published NASA and ESA research to examine challanges such as bone density loss, kidney stone formation, radiation-related biological changes, and neuronal oxidative stress.
Through interactive visualization, scientific comparisons, and countermeasure scenarios, users can explore how spaceflight conditions affect biological systems and how different preventive approaches may help reduce these risks.
Unlike conventional personal health monitoring applications, SpaceHealth-Sentinel
focused on research-based, mission-level understanding rather than predicting individual astronaut health outcomes.
My goal is to make complex space biology research more accessible, support evidence-informed countermeasure exploration, and contribute to safer future human space exploration.
details:
SpaceHealth-Sentinel is an interactive scientific research platform that examines biological and neurological risks associated with spaceflight using published NASA and ESA research.

The platform focuses on three research areas: bone density loss, kidney stone risk, and neurological oxidative stress. It presents scientific findings through interactive charts and examines the biological mechanisms behind these risks.

Users can explore published experimental results, compare preventive countermeasures, and investigate how different approaches may influence spaceflight-related health risks.

The project was developed using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, and Plotly. It combines scientific evidence, interactive data analysis, and research-based comparisons in an accessible web application.

SpaceHealth-Sentinel is designed for scientific exploration and education. It does not provide personalized medical predictions or claim to validate new medical treatments.
